sentences.japanese: 肉は食べないんです。
sentences.english: The thing is, I don't eat meat.

sentences.japanese: この靴は歩きやすいです。
sentences.english: These shoes are easy to walk in.

sentences.japanese: この漢字は読みにくいです。
sentences.english: This kanji is hard to read.

sentences.japanese: 先生の話は分かりやすいです。
sentences.english: The teacher's talk is easy to understand.

sentences.japanese: このペンは書きにくいですね。
sentences.english: This pen is hard to write with, isn't it?

sentences.japanese: 冬は朝起きにくいです。
sentences.english: In winter it's hard to get up in the morning.

sentences.japanese: その箸は使いやすいですか。
sentences.english: Are those chopsticks easy to use?

sentences.japanese: 昨日買ったかばんは持ちやすいです。
sentences.english: The bag I bought yesterday is easy to carry.

sentences.japanese: この地図は分かりにくいので、使いません。
sentences.english: This map is hard to understand, so I don't use it.

sentences.japanese: この皿は壊れやすいです。
sentences.english: This plate breaks easily.

sentences.japanese: 日本語の歌は覚えやすいですか。
sentences.english: Are Japanese songs easy to memorize?

sentences.japanese: 私の町は変わりつつある。
sentences.english: My town is changing.

sentences.japanese: 経済が悪くなりつつある。
sentences.english: The economy is gradually getting worse.

sentences.japanese: 会社の仕事が増えつつある。
sentences.english: The work at the company is steadily increasing.

sentences.japanese: 日が沈みつつある。
sentences.english: The sun is going down.

sentences.japanese: 雨が強くなりつつある。
sentences.english: The rain is getting heavier.

sentences.japanese: 日本語が上手になりつつあると思います。
sentences.english: I think my Japanese is getting better.

sentences.japanese: 森が無くなりつつあると聞きました。
sentences.english: I heard the forests are disappearing.

sentences.japanese: 雪が溶けつつあるのを見ました。
sentences.english: I watched the snow melting away.

sentences.japanese: 母の病気は治りつつあるでしょうか。
sentences.english: Is my mother's illness getting better, I wonder?

sentences.japanese: 店が減りつつあるので、町に人が来ない。
sentences.english: Shops are disappearing, so people don't come to town.

sentences.japanese: 財布を長い時間探したあげくに、見つかりませんでした。
sentences.english: After searching for my wallet for a long time, in the end I couldn't find it.

sentences.japanese: 財布を探したあげくに、犬のかばんの中から見つかりました。
sentences.english: After searching for my wallet, in the end it turned up inside the dog's bag.

sentences.japanese: 頑張ったあげく、困りました。
sentences.english: After trying so hard, in the end I was in trouble.

sentences.japanese: 雨の中で待ったあげく、バスは来ませんでした。
sentences.english: After waiting in the rain, in the end the bus never came.

alternates.japanese: 雨の中で待ったあげくに、バスは来ませんでした。

sentences.japanese: 何を買うか長く悩んだあげく、何も買いませんでした。
sentences.english: After agonizing for a long time over what to buy, in the end I bought nothing.

sentences.japanese: 色々な店を回ったあげく、最初の店で買いました。
sentences.english: After going around all sorts of shops, in the end I bought it at the first one.

alternates.japanese: 色々な店を回ったあげくに、最初の店で買いました。

sentences.japanese: 毎日練習したあげく、試験に落ちました。
sentences.english: After practicing every day, in the end I failed the exam.

sentences.japanese: 地図を見ながら歩いたあげく、道が分からなくなりました。
sentences.english: After walking while looking at the map, in the end I lost my way.

sentences.japanese: 長い間考えたあげく、行きませんでした。
sentences.english: After thinking it over for a long time, in the end I didn't go.

sentences.japanese: 今週は忙しいわけだ。
sentences.english: No wonder this week is busy.

sentences.japanese: 電車が遅れたわけだ。
sentences.english: So the train was late — that's what happened.

sentences.japanese: 彼は病気なわけだ。
sentences.english: So he's sick — that explains it.

sentences.japanese: 空が暗いから、雨が降るわけだ。
sentences.english: The sky's gone dark, so of course it's about to rain.

sentences.japanese: 雪が降っているから、寒いわけです。
sentences.english: It's snowing, so no wonder it's cold.

sentences.japanese: 彼は日本に住んでいたから、日本語が上手なわけです。
sentences.english: He lived in Japan, so it makes sense his Japanese is good.

alternates.japanese: 日本に住んでいたから、日本語が上手なわけです。

sentences.japanese: 毎日練習したから、上手になったわけだ。
sentences.english: You practiced every day, so that's why you got good.

sentences.japanese: だから、彼女は来なかったわけですか。
sentences.english: So that's why she didn't come?

sentences.japanese: 窓が開けてあるから、部屋が寒いわけです。
sentences.english: The window's been left open, so no wonder the room is cold.

sentences.japanese: 彼がそんな物を買うわけがありません。
sentences.english: There's no way he'd buy a thing like that.

alternates.japanese: 彼がそんな物を買うはずがありません。

sentences.japanese: こんなに簡単な問題が分からないわけがない。
sentences.english: There's no way you wouldn't understand such an easy problem.

sentences.japanese: 弟が自分で部屋を掃除したわけがない。
sentences.english: There's no way my little brother cleaned his room by himself.

sentences.japanese: 猫が英語を話すわけがない。
sentences.english: There's no way a cat can speak English.

alternates.japanese: 猫が英語を話すはずがない。

sentences.japanese: この店のケーキが安いわけがない。
sentences.english: There's no way this shop's cake is cheap.

sentences.japanese: 元気なわけがない。
sentences.english: There's no way he's doing fine.

sentences.japanese: 彼が忘れたわけがない。
sentences.english: There's no way he forgot.

alternates.japanese: 彼が忘れたはずがない。

sentences.japanese: そんなに早く宿題が終わるわけがありません。
sentences.english: There's no way the homework will be done that quickly.

sentences.japanese: あの優しい先生が怒るわけがない。
sentences.english: There's no way that gentle teacher would get angry.

sentences.japanese: 今日の試験はかなり難しかった。
sentences.english: Today's exam was quite difficult.

sentences.japanese: 彼はかなり足が速い。
sentences.english: He's quite a fast runner.

alternates.japanese: 彼は足がかなり速い。

sentences.japanese: 彼女はかなり親切だ。
sentences.english: She's quite kind.

sentences.japanese: 彼はご飯をかなり食べた。
sentences.english: He ate quite a lot of rice.

alternates.japanese: 彼はかなりご飯を食べた。

sentences.japanese: 彼はかなり忙しいから、あまり寝ない。
sentences.english: He's quite busy, so he doesn't sleep much.

sentences.japanese: この問題はかなり難しい。
sentences.english: This problem is quite difficult.

sentences.japanese: この部屋はかなり寒いですね。
sentences.english: This room is pretty cold, isn't it?

sentences.japanese: 今日はかなり歩きました。
sentences.english: I walked quite a lot today.

sentences.japanese: 駅までかなり遠いですか。
sentences.english: Is it quite far to the station?

sentences.japanese: 彼ほど頑張っている人はいません。
sentences.english: There's no one who works as hard as him.

sentences.japanese: 練習すればするほど、上手になります。
sentences.english: The more you practice, the better you get.

sentences.japanese: これはそれほど難しくない
sentences.english: This one isn't as difficult as that one.

sentences.japanese: 足が痛くなるほど歩いた
sentences.english: I walked until my feet hurt.

sentences.japanese: 声が出ないほど笑った
sentences.english: I laughed until my voice gave out.

sentences.japanese: 考えれば考えるほど分からなくなる
sentences.english: The more I think about it, the less I understand.

sentences.japanese: 話せば話すほど楽しくなる
sentences.english: The more we talk, the more fun it gets.

sentences.japanese: 泣くほど痛かったですか。
sentences.english: Did it hurt so much that you cried?

sentences.japanese: 今日は昨日ほど寒くないです。
sentences.english: Today isn't as cold as yesterday.

sentences.japanese: 宿題が山ほどあります。
sentences.english: I have a mountain of homework.

alternates.japanese: 山ほど宿題があります。

sentences.japanese: 泣きたいくらい嬉しいです。
sentences.english: I'm so happy I could cry.

sentences.japanese: 声が出なくなるくらい歌いました。
sentences.english: We sang until we lost our voices.

sentences.japanese: 前が見えないくらい雪が降りました。
sentences.english: It snowed so hard I couldn't see ahead.

sentences.japanese: 頭が痛くなるくらい忙しかった。
sentences.english: I was so busy my head started to hurt.

sentences.japanese: これくらいの雨なら傘は要らない。
sentences.english: If it's only about this much rain, you don't need an umbrella.

sentences.japanese: 少しくらい手伝ってくれてもいい。
sentences.english: You could at least help a little.

sentences.japanese: このカレーは口が痛いくらい辛いです。
sentences.english: This curry is so spicy it makes my mouth hurt.

alternates.japanese: このカレーは口が痛いぐらい辛いです。

sentences.japanese: 寝るのを忘れるくらい面白い本ですか。
sentences.english: Is it a book so good you forget to sleep?

sentences.japanese: あの店ぐらいおいしいラーメンはありません。
sentences.english: No ramen is as good as that shop's.

alternates.japanese: あの店くらいおいしいラーメンはありません。
あの店ほどおいしいラーメンはありません。

sentences.japanese: 英語だけでなく、日本語も勉強しました。
sentences.english: I studied not only English but Japanese too.

alternates.japanese: 英語だけじゃなく、日本語も勉強しました。

sentences.japanese: 彼は頭がいいだけでなく、優しいです。
sentences.english: He's not only smart, but also kind.

sentences.japanese: このレストランは安いだけでなく、おいしいです。
sentences.english: This restaurant isn't only cheap — it's delicious too.

sentences.japanese: 日本語は難しいだけでなく、面白い。
sentences.english: Japanese isn't only difficult — it's interesting too.

alternates.japanese: 日本語は難しいだけじゃなく、面白い。

sentences.japanese: 彼は先生だけでなく、医者でもあります。
sentences.english: He isn't only a teacher — he's also a doctor.

sentences.japanese: 彼は親切なだけでなく、有名だ。
sentences.english: He isn't only kind — he's also famous.

sentences.japanese: 高いだけじゃなく、まずい。
sentences.english: It's not only expensive — it's bad-tasting too.

alternates.japanese: 高いだけでなく、まずい。

sentences.japanese: 今日は忙しいだけでなく、宿題も多い。
sentences.english: Today isn't only busy — there's a lot of homework too.

sentences.japanese: 彼女は歌だけでなく、ダンスも上手ですか。
sentences.english: Is she good not only at singing but at dancing too?

sentences.japanese: 弟は肉だけでなく、野菜も食べない。
sentences.english: My little brother won't eat meat, and he won't eat vegetables either.

sentences.japanese: 日本に限らず、世界の人は寿司が好きです。
sentences.english: Not just in Japan — people all over the world like sushi.

sentences.japanese: 動物が好きなのは女の子に限らず、男の子も好きです。
sentences.english: Liking animals isn't limited to girls — boys like them too.

sentences.japanese: 忙しいのは会社員に限らず、学生も忙しいです。
sentences.english: Being busy isn't limited to office workers — students are busy too.

sentences.japanese: 病気になるのは大人に限らず、子供もなります。
sentences.english: Getting sick isn't limited to adults — children get sick too.

sentences.japanese: 環境問題は日本に限らず、世界の問題です。
sentences.english: Environmental problems aren't limited to Japan — they're a global issue.

sentences.japanese: 夏に限らず、冬もこの海に来る人が多い。
sentences.english: Not just in summer — lots of people come to this sea in winter too.

sentences.japanese: 先週は週末に限らず、毎日雨が降った。
sentences.english: Last week it rained every day, not just on the weekend.

sentences.japanese: その歌は若い人に限らず、みんなが知っていますか。
sentences.english: Does everyone know that song, not just young people?

sentences.japanese: お酒に限らず、彼女は甘い飲み物も飲まない。
sentences.english: It's not just alcohol — she doesn't drink sweet drinks either.

sentences.japanese: 便利な一方で、値段が高いです。
sentences.english: It's convenient, but on the other hand, it's expensive.

sentences.japanese: 兄はよく働く一方で、弟はあまり働かない。
sentences.english: My older brother works a lot; my younger brother, on the other hand, doesn't work much.

sentences.japanese: 部屋は広い一方で、駅から遠いです。
sentences.english: The room is spacious, but on the other hand it's far from the station.

alternates.japanese: 部屋は広いのに、駅から遠いです。

sentences.japanese: 兄は料理が上手な一方で、妹は下手です。
sentences.english: My older brother is good at cooking, but on the other hand my younger sister is bad at it.

sentences.japanese: その店は安い一方で、汚いです。
sentences.english: That shop is cheap, but on the other hand it's dirty.

sentences.japanese: 姉は真面目な一方で、厳しいです。
sentences.english: My older sister is serious, but on the other hand she's strict.

sentences.japanese: 姉は大学を卒業した一方で、兄はまだ学生です。
sentences.english: My older sister graduated from university, while my older brother is still a student.

sentences.japanese: この町は静かな一方で、不便ですか。
sentences.english: This town is quiet, but is it inconvenient on the other hand?

sentences.japanese: この仕事は面白い一方で、とても忙しいです。
sentences.english: This job is interesting, but on the other hand it's very busy.

sentences.japanese: 赤ちゃんにとって、この部屋は寒いです。
sentences.english: This room is cold for a baby.

sentences.japanese: この映画は君にとって面白い。
sentences.english: This movie is interesting to you.

sentences.japanese: 私にとって、日本語の勉強は大変だ。
sentences.english: Studying Japanese is tough for me.

sentences.japanese: この仕事は彼にとって簡単だ。
sentences.english: This job is easy for him.

sentences.japanese: この問題は先生にとっても難しかった。
sentences.english: This problem was hard even for the teacher.

sentences.japanese: あなたにとって、いい先生はどんな人ですか。
sentences.english: To you, what makes a good teacher?

sentences.japanese: この荷物は父にとって重くない。
sentences.english: This luggage isn't heavy for my father.

sentences.japanese: 猫にとって、箱は家です。
sentences.english: To a cat, a box is a home.

sentences.japanese: 外国人にとって、漢字は覚えにくい。
sentences.english: For foreigners, kanji are hard to memorize.

sentences.japanese: 環境に関して、色々な意見があります。
sentences.english: There are various opinions regarding the environment.

alternates.japanese: 環境について、色々な意見があります。

sentences.japanese: 会議で、部長は文化に関して質問した。
sentences.english: At the meeting, the department head asked a question about culture.

alternates.japanese: 会議で、部長は文化について質問した。

sentences.japanese: この問題に関して、先生は何も言いませんでした。
sentences.english: The teacher said nothing about this problem.

alternates.japanese: この問題について、先生は何も言いませんでした。

sentences.japanese: 健康に関する本を読みました。
sentences.english: I read a book about health.

sentences.japanese: 旅行に関して、何か質問はありますか。
sentences.english: Do you have any questions regarding the trip?

alternates.japanese: 旅行について、何か質問はありますか。

sentences.japanese: 日本の文化に関する記事は面白いです。
sentences.english: Articles about Japanese culture are interesting.

sentences.japanese: 天気に関するニュースを見ませんでした。
sentences.english: I didn't see the news about the weather.

sentences.japanese: 安全に関して、店の人に話を聞きました。
sentences.english: I asked the shop staff about safety.

alternates.japanese: 安全について、店の人に話を聞きました。

sentences.japanese: 歴史に関する話は、あまり面白くない。
sentences.english: Talk about history isn't very interesting.

sentences.japanese: こういう問題は難しいです。
sentences.english: This kind of problem is difficult.

sentences.japanese: そういう人は嫌いです。
sentences.english: I don't like that kind of person.

sentences.japanese: こういう天気は苦手だ。
sentences.english: I'm no good with this kind of weather.

sentences.japanese: 彼はそういう人だ。
sentences.english: He's that kind of person.

sentences.japanese: こういう話は前からあった。
sentences.english: This kind of story has been around for a while.

sentences.japanese: ああいう店に行きたいです。
sentences.english: I want to go to a shop like that one.

sentences.japanese: そういう話は聞きませんでした。
sentences.english: I didn't hear anything like that.

sentences.japanese: どうして、そういう物を買ったの？
sentences.english: Why did you buy that kind of thing?

alternates.japanese: どうしてそういう物を買ったの？

sentences.japanese: ああいう車は高いですか。
sentences.english: Is a car like that expensive?

sentences.japanese: こういう映画が好きです。
sentences.english: I like this kind of movie.

sentences.japanese: お兄さんって、優しいですね。
sentences.english: Your older brother is kind, isn't he.

alternates.japanese: お兄さんは、優しいですね。

sentences.japanese: 明日雨が降るって聞きました。
sentences.english: I heard it's going to rain tomorrow.

alternates.japanese: 明日雨が降ると聞きました。

sentences.japanese: 兄が忙しいって言ってた。
sentences.english: My older brother said he's busy.

sentences.japanese: それって面白い？
sentences.english: Is that thing interesting?

alternates.japanese: それは面白い？

sentences.japanese: これって面白いよね。
sentences.english: This is interesting, right?

alternates.japanese: これは面白いよね。

sentences.japanese: あれって難しい？
sentences.english: Is that thing over there hard?

alternates.japanese: あれは難しい？

sentences.japanese: 学校を休むって言った。
sentences.english: He said he'd skip school.

alternates.japanese: 学校を休むと言った。

sentences.japanese: 先生が優しいって。
sentences.english: The teacher is kind, they say.

sentences.japanese: この店のパンって、おいしい？
sentences.english: Is the bread at this shop any good?

alternates.japanese: この店のパンは、おいしい？

sentences.japanese: 猫って、本当に魚が好きだね。
sentences.english: Cats really do love fish, don't they.

alternates.japanese: 猫は、本当に魚が好きだね。

sentences.japanese: 弟ったら、また傘を忘れたの？
sentences.english: Ugh, my little brother — did he forget his umbrella again?

alternates.japanese: 弟ってば、また傘を忘れたの？

sentences.japanese: 兄ったら、話を全然聞かない。
sentences.english: My older brother, seriously, doesn't listen at all.

alternates.japanese: 兄ってば、話を全然聞かない。

sentences.japanese: 彼ったら、いつも宿題を忘れる。
sentences.english: Him, honestly — he always forgets his homework.

alternates.japanese: 彼ってば、いつも宿題を忘れる。

sentences.japanese: 分かったってば。
sentences.english: I said I get it.

sentences.japanese: 要らないってば。
sentences.english: I said I don't need it.

sentences.japanese: 猫がまた花を壊したってば。
sentences.english: I'm telling you, the cat wrecked the flowers again.

sentences.japanese: 友達ってば、また遅刻した。
sentences.english: My friend, honestly, was late again.

alternates.japanese: 友達ったら、また遅刻した。

sentences.japanese: 今行くってば。
sentences.english: I said I'm coming now!

sentences.japanese: もう寝るってば。
sentences.english: I told you, I'm going to bed now.

sentences.japanese: 彼が来るかどうか分かりません。
sentences.english: I don't know whether he'll come or not.

alternates.japanese: 彼が来るか分かりません。

sentences.japanese: 友達が来るかどうか分からない。
sentences.english: I don't know whether my friend is coming or not.

alternates.japanese: 友達が来るか分からない。

sentences.japanese: 明日雨が降るかどうか分からない。
sentences.english: I don't know whether it will rain tomorrow or not.

alternates.japanese: 明日雨が降るか分からない。

sentences.japanese: 彼が学生かどうか分からない。
sentences.english: I don't know whether he is a student or not.

sentences.japanese: 試験に合格したかどうか、まだ分からない。
sentences.english: I still don't know whether I passed the exam or not.

sentences.japanese: でも、友達が本当に来るかどうか分からない。
sentences.english: But I still don't know whether my friend is really coming or not.

sentences.japanese: この服が好きかどうか、母に聞きました。
sentences.english: I asked my mother whether she likes these clothes.

alternates.japanese: この服が好きか、母に聞きました。

sentences.japanese: 明日の会議に出席するかどうか、決めましたか。
sentences.english: Have you decided whether you'll attend tomorrow's meeting?

sentences.japanese: 電車が来るかどうか、駅の人に聞いた。
sentences.english: I asked the station staff whether the train was coming.

alternates.japanese: 電車が来るか、駅の人に聞いた。

sentences.japanese: 明日は映画とかテレビとか見ませんか。
sentences.english: Want to watch stuff like a movie or TV tomorrow?

sentences.english: Do you like animals — dogs, cats, that sort of thing?

sentences.english: While it's convenient, there's also danger.

sentences.japanese: 彼は日本語を話せる反面、書くのが苦手だ。

sentences.english: I went to a new restaurant. The food was delicious. However, the price was very expensive.

sentences.english: I waited for my friend at the station. However, my friend didn't come.

sentences.japanese: 兄はいつも厳しい。ところが、今日は優しかった。
sentences.english: My older brother is always strict. However, today he was kind.

sentences.japanese: 手紙を送った。ところが、届かなかった。
sentences.english: I sent a letter. However, it didn't arrive.

sentences.japanese: 弟は野菜が嫌いだ。ところが、このサラダは全部食べた。
sentences.english: My little brother hates vegetables. Yet he ate this whole salad.

sentences.english: I left home early. However, the train was late.

sentences.japanese: このケーキは高いです。それでも買いますか。
sentences.english: This cake is expensive. Will you still buy it?

sentences.english: My older brother had a fever. Even so, he went to work.

sentences.english: It was raining. Even so, my brother went for a walk.

sentences.english: My brother took his medicine, but even then his fever didn't go down.

sentences.japanese: 天気は悪かった。それでも私たちは公園を歩いた。
sentences.english: The weather was bad. Even so, we walked through the park.

sentences.japanese: 毎日練習した。それでもピアノは上手にならなかった。
sentences.english: I practiced every day. Even so, I didn't get good at the piano.

sentences.japanese: このかばんは古い。それでもまだ使える。
sentences.english: This bag is old. Even so, it can still be used.

sentences.japanese: 彼女は忙しい。それでも毎晩電話をくれる。
sentences.english: She's busy. Even so, she calls me every night.

sentences.japanese: 道が分かりませんでした。そこで、地図を見ました。
sentences.english: I didn't know the way. So I looked at a map.

sentences.japanese: 雨が降った。そこで、近くの喫茶店に入った。
sentences.english: It rained. So I went into a nearby coffee shop.

sentences.english: My head hurt. So I took some medicine.

sentences.english: The train was late. So I took a taxi.

sentences.english: The weather was bad. So I took an umbrella and went out.

sentences.english: The room is dark. So I turn on the light.

sentences.english: My luggage was heavy. So I got a friend to help me.

sentences.english: The bus isn't coming. So what should we do?

sentences.english: It's snowing. Will the bus be late because of that?

sentences.english: The earthquake left many people in difficulty.

alternates.japanese: 地震によって、たくさんの人が困った。

sentences.japanese: 会議によって、新しい予定が決まった。
sentences.english: The new schedule was settled through the meeting.

sentences.japanese: 時間によって、このバスは駅に止まりません。
sentences.english: Depending on the time, this bus doesn't stop at the station.

sentences.japanese: この小説は若い女性によって書かれた。
sentences.english: This novel was written by a young woman.

sentences.japanese: 買い物のついでに、郵便局へ行きました。
sentences.english: While I was out shopping, I stopped by the post office.

alternates.japanese: 買い物のついでに、郵便局に行きました。

sentences.japanese: コンビニに行くついでに、牛乳を買いましょうか。
sentences.english: Since I'm going to the convenience store anyway, shall I buy some milk?

sentences.japanese: 買い物のついでに、図書館で本を返す。
sentences.english: While I'm out shopping, I'll return the books at the library.

sentences.japanese: 台所を掃除するついでに、冷蔵庫も洗う。
sentences.english: While I'm cleaning the kitchen, I'll wash out the fridge too.

sentences.japanese: 郵便局に行くついでに、銀行にもお金を出す。
sentences.english: While I'm at the post office, I'll also take out money at the bank.

sentences.japanese: 会社から帰るついでに、スーパーで野菜を買う。
sentences.english: On my way home from work, I'll buy vegetables at the supermarket.

sentences.japanese: 父は散歩するついでに、パンを買いました。
sentences.english: My father bought bread while he was out on his walk.

sentences.japanese: 友達に会うついでに、借りた本を返しました。
sentences.english: While I was meeting my friend, I returned the book I'd borrowed.

sentences.japanese: お茶を入れるついでに、私のも入れてくれる？
sentences.english: While you're making tea, will you make mine too?

sentences.japanese: 説明をよく聞いた上で、契約します。
sentences.english: I'll sign the contract after listening carefully to the explanation.

sentences.japanese: 書類を全部読んだ上で、決めます。
sentences.english: I will decide after I have read all the documents.

sentences.japanese: 家族とよく話し合った上で、お答えします。
sentences.english: I will answer once I have talked it over properly with my family.

sentences.japanese: 医者に聞いた上で、薬を飲みます。
sentences.english: I will take the medicine after checking with the doctor.

sentences.japanese: 値段をよく考えた上で、買います。
sentences.english: I will buy it after thinking the price over carefully.

sentences.japanese: 弁護士に聞いた上で、書類に署名しました。
sentences.english: I signed the papers after asking a lawyer.

sentences.japanese: 説明を読んだ上で、申し込みますか。
sentences.english: Will you apply after reading the explanation?

sentences.japanese: 妻と話し合った上で、田舎には引っ越しません。
sentences.english: After talking it over with my wife, I'm not moving to the countryside.

sentences.japanese: 地図をよく見た上で、出かけましょう。
sentences.english: Let's head out after taking a good look at the map.

sentences.japanese: 会議の最中に、携帯が鳴った。
sentences.english: My phone rang right in the middle of the meeting.

sentences.japanese: 昼ご飯を食べている最中に、部長が来た。
sentences.english: The department head showed up right in the middle of my lunch.

alternates.japanese: 昼ご飯を食べている間に、部長が来た。

sentences.japanese: 映画を見ている最中に、地震が起きた。
sentences.english: An earthquake hit right in the middle of the movie.

alternates.japanese: 映画を見ている間に、地震が起きた。

sentences.japanese: 食事の最中に、社長から電話が来た。
sentences.english: A call from the company president came in right in the middle of dinner.

sentences.japanese: 友達と電話している最中に、赤ちゃんが泣いた。
sentences.english: The baby cried right in the middle of my phone call with a friend.

sentences.japanese: 授業の最中に、携帯は使いません。
sentences.english: I don't use my phone in the middle of class.

sentences.japanese: 先生の話の最中に、寝ましたか。
sentences.english: Did you fall asleep right in the middle of the teacher's talk?

sentences.japanese: 試験の最中に、お腹が痛くなった。
sentences.english: My stomach started to hurt right in the middle of the exam.

sentences.japanese: 寝ている最中に、猫が顔の上に乗った。
sentences.english: Right in the middle of my sleep, the cat climbed onto my face.

sentences.japanese: 料理をしている最中に、卵を落とした。
sentences.english: I dropped an egg right in the middle of cooking.

sentences.japanese: 会議の場所および時間は、まだ決まっていません。
sentences.english: The meeting's location and time have not been decided yet.

sentences.japanese: 試験の結果および説明は、金曜日に伝えます。
sentences.english: The exam results and the explanation will be given on Friday.

alternates.japanese: 金曜日に、試験の結果および説明を伝えます。

sentences.japanese: 名前および住所を、ここに書きます。
sentences.english: You write your name and address here.

alternates.japanese: ここに名前および住所を書きます。

sentences.japanese: 学生および先生は、この入口から入ります。
sentences.english: Students and teachers enter through this entrance.

sentences.japanese: 書類および荷物は、受付に出します。
sentences.english: Documents and luggage are handed in at the reception desk.

sentences.japanese: 図書館では、飲み物および食べ物を売っていません。
sentences.english: The library doesn't sell drinks or food.

sentences.japanese: 日本の文化および歴史に興味がありますか。
sentences.english: Are you interested in Japanese culture and history?

sentences.japanese: 去年、輸出および輸入が増えました。
sentences.english: Last year, exports and imports went up.

alternates.japanese: 輸出および輸入が去年増えました。

sentences.japanese: 社員およびその家族は、この病院を使います。
sentences.english: Employees and their families use this hospital.

sentences.japanese: 環境および健康の問題を、専門家が説明しました。
sentences.english: An expert explained the environmental and health issues.

sentences.japanese: 先生は生徒の質問に対して丁寧に答えます。
sentences.english: The teacher answers students' questions politely.

sentences.japanese: 彼は動物に対してとても優しいです。
sentences.english: He is very gentle toward animals.

sentences.japanese: 彼の子供に対する態度は厳しいです。
sentences.english: His attitude toward the children is strict.

sentences.japanese: 私の意見に対して、彼女は反対しました。
sentences.english: In response to my opinion, she objected.

alternates.japanese: 彼女は私の意見に対して反対しました。

sentences.japanese: あの店員はどのお客さんに対しても親切です。
sentences.english: That clerk is kind toward every customer.

sentences.japanese: 弟は、親に対して全然謝りません。
sentences.english: My younger brother never apologizes to our parents.

sentences.japanese: 彼の説明に対して、みんなは質問しました。
sentences.english: In response to his explanation, everyone asked questions.

sentences.japanese: 社長に対して、どんな言葉を使いますか。
sentences.english: What kind of words do you use toward the company president?

sentences.japanese: 父は私の夢に対して何も言いませんでした。
sentences.english: My father said nothing about my dream.

sentences.japanese: その質問に対する答えが分かりません。
sentences.english: I don't know the answer to that question.
